question: Which statement best describes A rule?
options: A selector chooses which HTML elements receive a rule. `.notice` selects elements carrying the `notice` class. It is like putting the same label on several boxes. Use classes for reusable component styles, and keep selectors simple so a rule does not affect unrelated parts of the page.

A property names the visual setting, such as `color`, `padding`, or `display`; its value tells the browser what to use. For example, `padding: 1rem` adds space inside a box. It is like choosing a setting and then choosing its amount. Invalid values may cause the browser to ignore a declaration.

A CSS rule has a selector and declarations. In `p { color: navy; }`, `p` selects paragraphs and the declaration sets their color. It is like an instruction with a target and a change. Braces hold the declarations together. A rule can contain several properties, such as color and line-height.

The cascade decides which matching rule supplies a property when several rules apply. Importance, selector specificity, and source order all matter. It is like resolving instructions by priority and then by which instruction came later. If the result surprises you, inspect the computed style to see which rule won.
